title: Meta Bans TikTok/ByteDance Ads
summary: Gotrade News - Meta Platforms (META) has banned advertising from ByteDance, the Chinese parent of TikTok, on Facebook and Instagram in the US and six
body_markdown:
## Why the Meta and TikTok Feud Escalated


Bloomberg reported that tensions had already been building before the ban. TikTok removed Instagram links from user profiles and rejected Meta's own advertisements, according to the report, turning a product rivalry into a dispute over which platform will carry the other's promotions.


TikTok is one of Meta's most formidable competitors for user engagement, creators and advertising revenue, per Reuters. In the US, TikTok operates as a majority American-owned joint venture with more than 200 million US users, according to the Investing.com report.


## The $18 Billion Child-Safety Settlement Behind the Fight


The ad ban follows Meta's $18 billion settlement with US states over social media harms to children. As reported by Bloomberg, Meta agreed in August to add new safety features for minors on Instagram and Facebook, and Reuters reported that the settlement requires daily usage limits and nighttime restrictions for minors.


Since then, Meta has pressed rivals to adopt comparable measures. Per Bloomberg, Meta pushed both TikTok and YouTube, owned by[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) , to implement similar child-safety steps, ran newspaper ads urging TikTok to comply, and publicly criticized TikTok for skipping a Surgeon General event on screen-time harms and withdrawing from a House Select Committee on China meeting.


TikTok reached its own separate settlement with Alabama in September over user-safety measures, according to the Investing.com report.


## Platforms Turning Away Rival Ads


Meta is not the first large tech company to refuse ads from competitors. Bloomberg noted that OpenAI rejected ads for competing image and audio-generation products, as reported in September 2026. Meta's own justification, in Sgro's words, is that turning away a rival's promotion is standard practice across industries.
